subject: KMS operator oral attestation and transport sampling
messages:
From: Alex Hansen <alex.hansen@frostbank.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: FrostBank Security <security@frostbank.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: KMS operator oral attestation and transport sampling

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the deep dive last week. As part of FrostBank's SIG review we need a short oral attestation from a Redwood KMS operator about operator controls (split duties, console access, emergency rotation) and a sample of transport manifests for the last month showing encrypted key movement between zones (S3 manifests or similar).

Specifically we need:
- A 10–20 minute remote interview with the operator who runs day-to-day KMS/HSM operations; a short consent stub is fine.
- A sampling of transport manifests (PDF/CSV) for up to 5 transfers in the last 30 days, redacted for tenant identifiers.
- A one-page summary of how emergency KEK rotation is performed (steps and roles).

Can you confirm availability this week and whether Redwood can provide the interview and the artifacts by EOD Friday (2026-11-05)?

Best,
Alex Hansen
Senior Information Security Manager
FrostBank
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Hansen <alex.hansen@frostbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: KMS operator oral attestation and transport sampling

Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. We can accommodate everything. Quick notes:
- Operator interview: we can arrange a remote session with an operator who routinely performs rotation and transport tasks. We will record a consent stub from the operator before the call and provide the transcript.
- Sample manifests: we'll provide redacted transport manifests (S3 transfer manifests and internal transfer logs) for up to 5 recent events.
- Emergency KEK rotation: I'll attach a concise one-page runbook.

I'll loop in our Cloud Ops lead (Irene) to schedule the interview window — does 11/03 09:00–11:00 PT or 11/04 13:00–15:00 PT work for you?

Deliverables ETA: We'll aim to share the artifact bundle and interview consent by EOD 2026-11-05. If you need faster turnaround on any item, let me know which has top priority.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments (will follow): operator_interview_consent.txt, kms_access_log_sample.csv, s3_transport_manifest.pdf
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Hansen <alex.hansen@frostbank.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: KMS operator oral attestation and transport sampling

Alex —

Thanks — I can host the interview and will be the technical interviewer. A few operational clarifications up-front so the interview is focused:
1) The operator we'll present is a shift lead with console R/W restrictions managed through RBAC; we can speak to separation of duties and our session recording/approval process.
2) The sample manifests will be redacted for customer and tenant IDs; we will include checksums and transfer timestamps.
3) Emergency KEK rotation is typically executed via a scripted playbook initiated from the orchestration plane; the operator performs verification steps and notifies Security for a coordinated rollback plan.

Irene
Director, Cloud Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Hansen <alex.hansen@frostbank.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: SecureScan Audit <audit@securescan.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 11:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: KMS operator oral attestation and transport sampling

Soojin / Irene —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. 11/04 13:00 PT works. Please confirm the dial-in link and whether the interview will be recorded (consent is required). SecureScan will attend to observe. For artifacts: if you can prioritize the manifests and the KEK rotation summary, we can review interview notes afterward.

Also: can you provide a small sample of the operator's access audit (console session start/stop lines) for the same transfer events? We only need a few lines per event (timestamps and user id).

Appreciate it,
Alex
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Hansen <alex.hansen@frostbank.com>, SecureScan Audit <audit@securescan.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 16:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: KMS operator oral attestation and transport sampling

Alex / Audit team —

Follow-up and delivery notes (per our commitments):

1) Interview: Completed 2026-11-04 13:05 PT. Operator interview conducted by Irene Choi; SecureScan observed. We recorded the session after confirming consent; transcript and consent stub attached (operator_interview_consent.txt).

2) Manifests: Delivered redacted transport manifests for 4 transfers in the last 30 days (s3_transport_manifest.pdf). Each manifest includes transfer id, timestamp, source/destination zone (redacted), and SHA256 checksum of the bundle.

3) Access audit snippets: kms_access_log_sample.csv contains the session start/stop and minimal operator IDs for the same transfer events (redacted user hashes).

4) KEK rotation summary: Attached is a one-page runbook outlining roles, approval gates, and verification steps. We included a brief note on fallback and rollback timing (<= 15 minutes to stage rollback).

Related links:
- Internal artifact bundle (read-only): https://redwood-internal.fwd/drive/kms-snapshot-20261101
- HubSpot record: HB-9923

Attachments: operator_interview_consent.txt (text), kms_access_log_sample.csv (CSV stub), s3_transport_manifest.pdf (PDF stub)

If the audit team needs a live walk-through of any specific transfer or an expanded audit extract, flag which event IDs you'd like unredacted under an NDA and we'll assemble that package.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
